metadata.title: Historical Chart Sources & Calculation Methodology | BTLLC

description: How we sample LBMA prices, calculate changes and ratios, and adjust gold for inflation. Data coverage, observation dates and limitations.
text:
← Historical charts
Historical chart methodology
One monthly observation is useful for showing a long history. It does not describe every trade or every day's high and low.
Prepared by the
Bullion Trading LLC editorial team
. Dataset retrieved
2026-09-26
. Retrieval time is not the observation date or a claim that the series is live.
Sources and coverage
Our historical series uses the
LBMA precious-metal benchmark prices
supplied by its historical price feed. Gold, platinum and palladium use the PM observation; silver uses its daily observation. Values are per troy ounce in the currency provided by the source. EUR observations begin in 1999; missing values are omitted, not treated as zero.

Monthly observations and incomplete periods
We select the last available daily fixing in each calendar month. The newest month may be incomplete and changes when more data becomes available. A past month is only as complete as the source data. The date shown beside an observation is the actual fixing date, not the first day of the month or the page-build date.
Highs and lows on monthly charts are the largest and smallest sampled observations. An “all-time-high” URL is retained for existing links, but its page reports the highest monthly sample. Daily or intraday market records can differ. For a particular day's fixing, use the
daily lookup
.
Changes and averages
Change = (last available observation ÷ first available observation − 1) × 100. The yearly table's first point is normally the last available January fixing, not the opening price on January 1. This is not a calendar-year investment return. Current years and decades are partial. The mean is the arithmetic average of the available monthly observations, not an average of all daily prices.
Gold-to-silver ratio
We divide the monthly gold observation by the silver observation for the same month and currency. Fixing dates can differ when a source has gaps, and the metals' benchmarks are set at different times of day. This is not a simultaneous tradable quote. The percentile is the share of sampled ratios at or below the latest ratio; it does not predict future returns.
Inflation adjustment
Real price = nominal monthly price × CPI-U for 2026-08 ÷ CPI-U for the observation month. We use the
BLS CPI-U
all-items US city average, not seasonally adjusted (CUUR0000SA0). 2026-08 is the reference month, not “today's dollars.” Months without matching CPI data are omitted.
Gold and the S&P 500
The comparison aligns available monthly observations and rebases both series to 100 at the first shared point. The S&P 500 series is a price index, excluding dividends. Gold prices exclude dealer premiums, storage, insurance and transaction costs. The chart is not a comparison of net investor returns.
Historical benchmarks and retail quotes
These datasets update when new data is published to this site. They are separate from the
live spot dashboard
. A retail bullion quote also depends on the product, quantity, premium and payment method. See the product page and checkout for the applicable purchase price.
To report a data issue, include the chart URL, metal, currency and observation date when contacting
[email protected]
.
